sanskrit_verse:
सिंहव्याघ्रहतो वापि व्यादिभिः चैव पातितः।
न तत्र दोषः पालस्य न च दोषोऽस्ति गोमिनाम्॥
transliteration: siṃhavyāghrahato vāpi vyādhibhiḥ caiva pātitaḥ | na tatra doṣaḥ pālasya na ca doṣo 'sti gominām ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When a cow perishes due to lions, tigers, or diseases, neither the protector nor the owner incurs fault.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is not liable when causation originates beyond human control.
Responsibility aligns with capacity to prevent harm.
Restoration arises through understanding natural and unavoidable causality.
Consciousness alignment occurs by recognizing non-agentic forces in outcome determination.
executable_legal_axioms: IF harm occurs due to non-human or uncontrollable natural causes THEN no legal liability attaches to custodians or owners.
IF causation chain includes exclusively non-agentic factors THEN responsibility does not arise for sentient guardians.
IF damage results from forces beyond prevention capacity THEN restoration bypasses attribution of fault.
supreme_court_application: In cases where loss or injury stems from forces entirely outside human agency—such as wild animals or disease—the Supreme Court must recognize absence of actionable liability. The threshold of responsibility requires capacity to intervene; when absent, no judicial penalty applies.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality was neither initiated nor preventable by the involved parties. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals sequential unfolding without sentient interference. Therefore, proportional responsibility is nullified. This aligns with the non-punitive reality rule: no suffering is assigned where consciousness had no operative role.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process involves acknowledgment of natural causality.
No obligation imposed on guardian or owner beyond factual reporting.
Community support activated for material replacement if needed.
Integrity reintegration achieved through reaffirmation of dharma-sustained roles.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: where causation lies outside human agency, there is no fault, no liability, no punishment. Dharma prevails through recognition of rightful order. Consciousness alone is the ultimate judge.
